first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, so simplifying onboarding targets two immediate constraints and has prior evidence of improving completion, time-to-value, and early adoption. Verify the two onboarding-related records for durability and segment fit, and verify promotional pricing as the strongest alternative because it directly addresses competitive pressure but may create discounting, customer-quality, or retention risk that matters for sustainable qualified revenue.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening onboarding. It directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also recover activation, with confirmed evidence of +13% completion, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention. Signup simplification provides additional SMB evidence of activation and qualified-revenue lift, though its slight retention decline warrants monitoring. Promotional pricing is rejected despite acquisition lift because the verified cohort had materially worse retention and failed to survive the first renewal cycle, conflicting with sustainable long-term qualified revenue.
